questions.q: I ___ in this city for ten years, and I still live here.
questions.why: Present perfect links a past start to the present for an unfinished situation.

questions.q: We ___ to Paris last summer.
questions.why: Past simple is used with a finished time expression like 'last summer'.

questions.q: She has worked here ___ 2019.
questions.why: 'Since' is used with a point in time when the action started.

questions.q: They have been married ___ twenty years.
questions.why: 'For' is used with a length or period of time.

questions.q: Have you finished your homework ___?
questions.why: 'Yet' is used in questions and negatives to ask about expected completion.

questions.q: I've ___ eaten, thanks, so I'm not hungry.
questions.why: 'Already' shows something happened sooner than expected.

questions.q: ___ you ever ___ sushi?
questions.why: Present perfect with 'ever' asks about life experience up to now.

questions.q: I have ___ been to Japan, so I don't know what it's like.
questions.why: 'Never' with present perfect means 'not at any time in my life'.

questions.q: Where's Tom? He ___ to the bank; he'll be back soon.
questions.why: 'Has gone' means he is still away at the destination.

questions.q: Sarah looks tanned. She ___ to the beach.
questions.why: 'Has been' means she went and has now returned.

questions.q: I ___ my keys this morning, but I found them.
questions.why: 'This morning' is finished now (said later), so past simple fits.

questions.q: I ___ three coffees today, and the day isn't over.
questions.why: 'Today' is unfinished time, so present perfect is used.

questions.q: He ___ his leg, so he can't play today.
questions.why: Present perfect connects a past action to a present result.

questions.q: Shakespeare ___ many famous plays.
questions.why: Past simple is used because the person's life is finished.

questions.q: The train ___ just ___; you missed it.
questions.why: 'Just' with present perfect means a very short time ago.

questions.q: I ___ that film three times.
questions.why: Present perfect describes repeated experience in a time up to now.

questions.q: When ___ you ___ your driving test?
questions.why: 'When' asks about a definite past time, so use past simple.

questions.q: It's the best meal I ___ ever ___.
questions.why: Present perfect with superlatives describes experience up to the present.

questions.q: We haven't seen each other ___ we left school.
questions.why: 'Since' introduces the point in the past when something began.

questions.q: I met my wife two years ___.
questions.why: 'Ago' measures back from now and takes past simple.

questions.q: ___ she finished the report yet?
questions.why: Present perfect questions with 'yet' use 'has/have' plus the past participle.

questions.q: Did you call him ___?
questions.why: Past simple pairs with a finished time word like 'yesterday'.

questions.q: They ___ the house in 1990 and sold it in 2005.
questions.why: Two finished past dates require past simple throughout.

questions.q: I've known her ___ we were children.
questions.why: 'Since' is followed by a clause stating when the action began.

questions.q: Oh no, I ___ my coffee all over the keyboard!
questions.why: Present perfect emphasises a recent action with a present consequence.

questions.q: My grandfather ___ in the war when he was young.
questions.why: A completed past period in a finished life takes past simple.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'I have known him ___ five years.' (for/since)
questions.why: 'For' is used with a duration of time.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'She has lived here ___ 2010.' (for/since)
questions.why: 'Since' is used with the point when something started.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'Where's Mum? She has ___ (go) shopping and isn't back yet.'
questions.why: 'Gone' shows the person is still away at the place.

questions.q: Type the answer: 'I ___ (see) that film yesterday.' (correct tense)
questions.why: 'Yesterday' is finished time, so past simple is required.
